quote: But then I have always supposed it to be my own fault—because I would not take the trouble of practising.
source: Jane Austen, Pride and Prejudice, ch. 31: vol. II, ch. 8 in the 1813 edition (Elizabeth Bennet, to Mr Darcy)

evidence.edition: Jane Austen, Pride and Prejudice (George Allen, 1894); Project Gutenberg #1342; first published by T. Egerton, 1813
evidence.locator: Chapter XXXI (volume II, chapter 8), at the pianoforte at Rosings, in the speech beginning “My fingers,” said Elizabeth, answering Darcy on conversing with strangers

reason: The sentence is verbatim in chapter 31, in Elizabeth’s speech to Darcy at the instrument, with the dash after “fault”. Not shipped; Austen has one line this year (February), none in March, under the cap; not banned.
